newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Poll close in Albania election.
newsitem.headline: Poll close in Albania election.

text.p: Polls closed on Sunday in Albania's general election after a day of voting marked by the death of one local official but free of the widespread violence which has gripped the country for months.

Polling stations were closed at 6 p.m. (1600 GMT), three hours earlier than planned under the electoral law. Major parties had agreed to the early closure to help ensure safety for voters and about 500 observers watching polling stations.
The official count was due to begin soon after the polls closed and some results might be available on Sunday evening.

Streets in Tirana were quiet and empty of residents who generally throng tree-lined boulevards for an evening stroll. Truckloads of armed police stood by in side streets off central Skanderbeg Square.

In southern Albania's Adriatic ports, focal point of months of violence, voting closed after a day almost free of incidents. One polling station in Sarande remained open after the deadline to enable a crowd of latecomers to vote.
In the day's most serious incident, a local election official was shot dead in a village near the southern city of Fier.
